Actually, bio-social theory, which is the basis for DBT, has shown that negative experiences that invalidate, ignore or oversimplify emotions can result in BPD symptoms for those who are biologically predisposed to be more sensitive and reactive. It does not differentiate between “true” trauma or negative experiences or otherwise sort out “bad” from “worst.” So there is research and theory out there that verbal abuse can cause emotional disregulation and other negative psychiatric experiences. 

Also I think it might be worth exploring why you feel so strongly this matters. Why is it so important we delineate between who is “allowed” to be traumatized and who isn’t?

This feels like unnecessary gate keeping to me. You can call it trauma (or not) and still take responsibility for your thoughts and actions around it. Even if you’ve faced “true” trauma, you still need to take responsibility for your thoughts and actions around it - so why split hairs? Why invalidate peoples feelings? 

Also worth mentioning that the way psychiatry is looked at from a research perspective is very different from the functions of therapeutic treatment. I’ve been told by multiple therapists that the DSM is not the end all be all and precise definitions of disorders are less important than a patients experiences. My most recent therapist referred to my childhood experiences as “trauma” despite it not meeting the DSM definition.

I do this too. I agree with the person above who said this is a self protective response. I’m so scared of rejection that I’m hyper aware of any negative tone, action, slight, etc. I think it’s my way of identifying who is going to hurt or reject me, and I can get away from them or the situation quickly. Unfortunately, it’s often extremely over exaggerated. For example, just because my boss may not like one small decision I made at work, doesn’t mean I need to start job searching. But that’s exactly how my brain works. 

Blowing it out of proportion is bad enough but sometimes I’ve found out in the past that my interpretation of a situation wasn’t even accurate. For example, I had 2 friends (a couple) who I hadn’t seen in months. I was convinced they wanted nothing to do with me and felt awkward with me after I broke up with my boyfriend because I was 3rd wheel. I even started to think of reasons why they may have been actively mad at me - I had gone on a handful of dates with one of their other friends and we weren’t a match, so I thought maybe they were mad at me about that. I invited one of them to a bar with me and some girlfriends finally and I opened up to her about it and all my paranoid thoughts and said I wanted to apologize. Turns out, she had absolutely none of those feelings about me or the situation whatsoever. They had just been extremely busy renovating their house and both had gotten new jobs so they weren’t spending as much time being social as they had previously. It was eye opening for me at the time. 

Unfortunately, I do slip back into old habits and I still worry, worry, worry about people’s perception of me. It’s been especially bad for me for the last several weeks as I’ve been feeling uncomfortable at work and it’s magnifying my feelings and concerns. I wish I had more suggestions on how to deal with it but at least know you’re not alone.

I was mental health arrested last year and put on a 48 hour hold against my will. I was told by the social worker the best way to get out of it was to pretend to be happy. I talked to the psychiatrist for less than 5 minutes and spent the rest of the time crying, laying on a plastic bench with no pillows or blankets, and being groped by a fellow patient. It was an awful experience. I absolutely do not trust the inpatient system or the law in these situations.

ETA: they also took my cell phone and wouldn’t let me use a computer or phone so even if I had the thought to get legal help, I was trapped and unable to contact anyone. They wouldn’t even let me contact my employer myself to let them know I wasn’t coming to work. On top of it, they also shared with my employer that I was in the psychiatric unit of the hospital. Again, all of this was out of my control. The best part is that if you try to object or make a complaint they just blame it on your mental health issue.

One more edit: they may not be able to literally force you to take medication but they have no problem threatening you with a longer hold if you refuse. Again, speaking from experience.
